_README: AsOtaIotPresignRole — the role AWS IoT Core assumes to SIGN the S3 URL inside ${aws:iot:s3-presigned-url:...}. Referenced by [iot].presign_role_arn and passed to CreateJob as presignedUrlConfig.roleArn. Without this role the placeholder is delivered to the device VERBATIM and every OTA fails at AT+QHTTPGET with HTTP 403. Create with: aws iam create-role --role-name AsOtaIotPresignRole --assume-role-policy-document file://trust_policy --- then attach permissions_policy.

Statement.Comment: GetObject on firmwares/ ONLY. Deliberately excludes jobs/ — the signing role has no reason to read job documents, and scoping it here means a leaked pre-signed URL can only ever expose a firmware image that is already being distributed to devices.

_NOTES: The trust policy uses aws:SourceAccount + aws:SourceArn to prevent the confused-deputy problem: without them, any AWS account whose IoT jobs reference this role ARN could have IoT sign objects in your bucket.
aws:SourceArn is pinned to the as-ota-* job prefix, matching make_job_id() in core/jobs.py.

expiresInSec (presign_expires_sec, default 3600) starts when the DEVICE fetches the job document, not at CreateJob. It only has to outlast one download; the EC200U path is QHTTPREADFILE to UFS then chunked QFREAD, typically well under 10 minutes on LTE.
If the bucket is SSE-KMS encrypted, add kms:Decrypt on the CMK to permissions_policy, or the signed URL will return 403 at the device.
